name: Cheltenham

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme: none is listed on the council’s private housing pages.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme is listed: the council’s HMO page describes national mandatory HMO licensing (five or more people from two or more households). An Article 4 direction in St Paul’s means converting a house to an HMO there needs planning permission.
licensing.fee: £400 (part 1) plus £570 (part 2) for a standard HMO licence, with extra charges for larger HMOs

housing: Cheltenham is known for its Regency architecture: large stucco terraces and villas in Montpellier, Pittville and the Suffolks, many of them listed and split into flats. Victorian terraces around St Paul's and the Tewkesbury Road area are let to students and young professionals, while the west of the town has post-war estates. New building has added apartment blocks in the centre and family estates on the edges. GCHQ, the University of Gloucestershire and the racecourse all add demand for lets.
checkinTips: Regency flats in Montpellier and Pittville: photograph sash windows and shutters, ornate ceilings, cornices and any cracks.
Listed buildings: record original features such as fireplaces and doors carefully, as changes may need consent.
Basement and lower-ground flats in the Regency terraces: check for damp, condensation and working extractor fans.
Shared houses near the University of Gloucestershire campuses: photograph each bedroom's lock, the fire doors, smoke alarms and the shared kitchen.
Communal hallways in converted villas: note shared meters, door entry systems, bins and the number of keys and fobs handed over.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a privately rented home can contact Cheltenham Borough Council's private sector housing team.
